name: The polar lights — aurora borealis & australis
scope: The polar lights: a curtain of colored light where the Sun's own particles pour into the sky. Spine = ONE process (solar wind -> Earth's magnetic field -> glowing high air), deepened across the named towns under the auroral oval. T1 (Tromso, Norway / Lapland): the green ribbon overhead is powered by PARTICLES FROM THE SUN (the solar wind) funneled down Earth's magnetic field — not by cold, snow-glare, or moonlight. T2: aurora rides a ring — the AURORAL OVAL — centered ~67 degrees around the magnetic pole, which is why Fairbanks (Alaska), Yellowknife (Canada) and Tromso sit in the 'aurora belt' and see it most clear nights. T3: the common green is OXYGEN glowing ~100 km up; the rare red crown on a towering aurora is oxygen 200+ km up; the purple-blue skirt along the bottom is NITROGEN (one gas/one color per rung — do not stack). T4: after a solar storm the lights 'explode' near midnight (a substorm); Abisko, Sweden's rain-shadow 'blue hole' keeps its patch of sky clear when everywhere else clouds over. T5: the SOUTHERN mirror — the aurora AUSTRALIS over Antarctica, Tasmania and southern New Zealand — flares at the very same instant as the north (conjugate auroras). T5+ payoff: STEVE — a mauve ribbon with a green 'picket fence,' spotted by Alberta aurora-chasers around 2016 and found to be not a true aurora at all but a 25-km-wide river of gas near 3,000 C streaming at several km per second.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurora (auroral oval ~67 deg, O 557.7nm green ~100km, O 630nm red 200+km, N blue/purple, borealis vs australis, substorm); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STEVE (Strong Thermal Emission Velocity Enhancement, Alberta Aurora Chasers 2016, ~25km ribbon, ~3000C, subauroral ion drift, picket fence). Named viewing sites (Tromso/Fairbanks/Yellowknife/Abisko) general geographic knowledge.
framing_note: Wonder voice, scene-led ('a green curtain ripples over Tromso...'), never 'What causes the aurora?'. Accuracy rail: green = atomic oxygen ~100 km, red = oxygen 200+ km, blue/purple = nitrogen — ONE gas per rung, never theory-stacked. Distractors are adjacent-real wrong causes/colors (reflected snow, moonlight, city glow; wrong gas). Dinner-test payoff = STEVE. Respect indigenous sky-lore (Sami, Cree, Maori Tahu-nui-a-rangi) as real culture, never 'primitive superstition' — but keep every KEYED answer the physics/place, folklore stays context. Aurora australis is the identical physics over the south; a concrete place name shows in every stem.

name: Where the Sun forgets to set — midnight sun & polar night
scope: Where the Sun forgets to set (or to rise). Spine = Earth's 23.5-degree tilt playing out across the named Arctic and Antarctic towns. T1 (North Cape / Nordkapp, Norway): the Sun still hangs above the horizon at MIDNIGHT in June — the 'midnight sun,' when for weeks the Sun never sets at all. T2: the cause is Earth's AXIAL TILT (~23.5 degrees) leaning the pole toward the Sun — NOT being 'closer to the Sun' (kill that common wrong idea here). T3: on Svalbard (Longyearbyen) the Sun does not set from about 19 April to 23 August — roughly FOUR MONTHS of unbroken daylight. T4: the flip side is the POLAR NIGHT — at Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska the Sun stays below the horizon for about 65 days (mid-November to late January), the town lit only by twilight, snow-glow and aurora. T5 payoff: stand at the POLE itself and the whole year is a single day and a single night — about six months of Sun, then about six months of dark (the North Pole gets ~186 sunlit days). T5+: Antarctica's research stations (McMurdo, Amundsen-Scott South Pole) live the southern version — a summer that never darkens, then the long winter night.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_sun (Arctic Circle boundary; Svalbard no-sunset ~19 Apr-23 Aug; North Cape ~14 May-29 Jul; axial tilt 23 deg 26 min; North Pole ~186 polar-day days, South Pole ~179). Utqiagvik polar-night span (~65 days) and Antarctic stations = general geographic knowledge (reconfirm at build).
framing_note: Scene-led ('the Sun rides above North Cape at 1 a.m.'), never 'What is the midnight sun?'. Accuracy rail: the cause is the 23.5-degree TILT, NOT distance to the Sun — make T2 explicitly defeat that misconception, and keep the Svalbard/Utqiagvik date-spans exact (reconfirm at build). Distractors adjacent-real (wrong cause: closer to Sun / faster spin / thinner air; wrong town/latitude). Dinner-test payoff = the Pole's single six-month day and six-month night.

name: The darkest skies on Earth — where the Milky Way casts a shadow
scope: The darkest skies on Earth, where the stars come flooding back. Spine = why a few dry, high, empty places give the blackest sky, deepened across the named dark-sky sites. T1 (Atacama, Chile): some stations here may have gone years — even, by some evidence, centuries — with almost no rain; it is the driest nonpolar desert, and that bone-dry, cloudless air makes it the planet's clearest window on the stars. T2: it is so dry because it is trapped in the ANDES' rain shadow and chilled by the cold Humboldt Current offshore (teach 'rain shadow'). T3: on the ~5,000 m Chajnantor Plateau stands ALMA (66 dishes listening to the cold universe); nearby Paranal holds the VERY LARGE TELESCOPE, with the Extremely Large Telescope rising close by. T4 payoff: in skies this dark the MILKY WAY casts a faint shadow on the ground — and on the very darkest nights the planet Venus can too. T5: NamibRand (Namibia) became Africa's first International Dark Sky Reserve, and Aoraki Mackenzie (New Zealand) is a whole reserve where the Southern Cross and the Magellanic Clouds blaze and the zodiacal light ('false dawn') stands up from the horizon. T5+: light pollution has erased the Milky Way for most people (around 80% of North Americans can no longer see it); the Bortle scale rates how dark a sky truly is.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atacama_Desert (driest nonpolar desert; Andes/Coast-Range rain shadow + Humboldt Current + South Pacific anticyclone; ALMA at Chajnantor ~5000m, VLT at Paranal, ELT at Cerro Armazones, 200+ cloudless nights). NamibRand & Aoraki Mackenzie IDA reserve status, Milky-Way/Venus shadow under Bortle-1, ~80% lost-Milky-Way stat = general knowledge (reconfirm at build).
framing_note: Wonder + honest-science voice; celebrate the great observatories as genuine human achievement. Scene-led, never 'What is the driest desert?' — invert: the near-rainless hook -> 'the Atacama.' Accuracy rail: the Milky-Way-casts-a-shadow and Venus-shadow claims hold only under a Bortle-1 sky — keep them tied to these darkest sites; reconfirm NamibRand (~2012, Africa's first) and Aoraki Mackenzie reserve status at build. Distractors adjacent-real (other deserts: Sahara/Gobi/Namib; other observatories: Mauna Kea/La Palma/Canary). Dinner-test payoff = the Milky Way casting a shadow. If a Mauna Kea rung is built, respect the sacred summit AND the astronomers on their own terms — no smug dismissal either way. Lane: the PLACE and its sky, not a stellar-astrophysics course.

name: The everlasting storm — Catatumbo lightning over Lake Maracaibo
scope: The everlasting storm: one place, one wonder — a sky that almost never stops flashing. T1 (mouth of the Catatumbo River, Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela): over this one spot storms flash almost every night — up to ~40 lightning bolts a MINUTE, about nine hours a night, 140-160 nights a year. T2: for centuries sailors steered by it — the near-constant glow, visible for hundreds of km, worked as a natural lighthouse the Spanish called the 'Beacon (Faro) of Maracaibo.' T3: why HERE — warm, moist air off the lake meets cool air spilling down the ANDES at night, and the ring of mountains funnels the storms back over the same water again and again (topography + wind convergence). T4: it holds the Guinness record for the highest lightning DENSITY on Earth — about 250 flashes per square km each year (the older 'swamp-methane' explanation is now disputed — label it, do not state it as fact). T5 payoff: in the 2010 drought the lightning nearly vanished for weeks and alarmed the whole region — proof the marvel hangs on the lake's exact climate; it also shines on the flag and coat of arms of Zulia state.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catatumbo_lightning (Lake Maracaibo / Catatumbo river mouth; 140-160 nights/yr, 9 hrs/night, 16-40 flashes/min; 250/km2/yr highest globally; Andes wind convergence; methane theory contested; 'Lighthouse of Maracaibo'; Zulia flag/coat of arms). 2010 pause = general knowledge (reconfirm at build).
framing_note: Scene-led wonder ('night after night the sky over Lake Maracaibo strobes...'), never 'Where is the most lightning on Earth?'. Invert the superlative: the flash-count hook -> a concrete answer (a natural lighthouse / the mountain-lake convergence). Accuracy rail: 140-160 nights, up to ~40 flashes/min, ~250/km2/yr (Guinness); the methane cause is DISPUTED. Distractors adjacent-real (other lightning capitals: Kifuka DR Congo, Lake Victoria basin, Florida; wrong cause). Dinner-test payoff = the 2010 disappearance (the fragile wonder) or the Beacon sailors steered by.

name: The sea that glows blue — bioluminescent bays
scope: The sea that glows blue at night. Spine = living light in the water, deepened across the named glowing bays. T1 (Mosquito Bay, Vieques, Puerto Rico): every stroke and splash lights up electric BLUE after dark — the water is packed with billions of dinoflagellates, single-celled plankton that flash when the water is disturbed. T2: Mosquito Bay is the BRIGHTEST bioluminescent bay in the world — because its narrow mouth and mangrove-lined shore trap the plankton so they pile up (the bay's geography makes the glow, not luck). T3: Puerto Rico has THREE such bays (Mosquito, Laguna Grande at Fajardo, La Parguera) — more than any country — and Jamaica's Luminous Lagoon is another Caribbean glow-water. T4: the Maldives' 'Sea of Stars' at Vaadhoo scatters blue sparks along the sand as each wave breaks. T5 payoff: Taiwan's Matsu Islands glow with 'blue tears' (a different plankton, Noctiluca) so bright that satellites catch it from orbit — beautiful, yet sometimes a warning sign of an algae bloom.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioluminescence (dinoflagellates cause sparkling glow in disturbed surface water; luciferin+O2->light; warm lagoons with narrow ocean openings concentrate them; milky seas). Mosquito Bay Guinness 'brightest' record, species Pyrodinium bahamense, Vaadhoo 'Sea of Stars', Matsu 'blue tears' = Noctiluca scintillans — all general knowledge, RECONFIRM at build.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder ('dip a paddle in Mosquito Bay and it blazes blue'), never 'What is bioluminescence?'. Accuracy rail: reconfirm at build — Mosquito Bay's Guinness 'brightest' record + species Pyrodinium bahamense; Matsu 'blue tears' = Noctiluca scintillans. Keep every ANSWER a PLACE-fact (which bay, why it concentrates there, the record), NOT organism anatomy. LANE BORDER: the plankton glow is a place-ecology fact and stays in geography; Toyama Bay's firefly-SQUID glow is an ANIMAL (animal bank) — use it only as a one-line contrast, never key its biology. Distractors adjacent-real (other bays/lagoons; wrong cause: reflected moonlight, phosphorus). Dinner-test payoff = Matsu's 'blue tears' seen from space.

name: A living night sky underground — the Waitomo glowworm caves
scope: A living night sky underground. Spine = the glowworm caves and the KARST that made them, anchored at Waitomo. T1 (Waitomo Caves, North Island, New Zealand): in one pitch-dark grotto the ceiling glitters with thousands of tiny blue-green lights, like a galaxy hung in the rock — the Glowworm Grotto. T2: the caves are LIMESTONE KARST — passages dissolved by water out of ~30-million-year-old (Oligocene) seabed rock, hung with stalactites and stalagmites (teach 'karst'). T3: you drift beneath the living lights by BOAT in silence, because noise and light make the glow fade. T4: the caves were first explored in 1887 by Maori chief Tane Tinorau with English surveyor Fred Mace, poling a flax raft by candlelight; the land was later returned to Tane's descendants, who own and run the caves today. T5 payoff: the glowworm Arachnocampa luminosa shines nowhere on Earth but the caves and wet forests of New Zealand — a light found only here (its few cousins glow in Australian karst caves such as Tasmania's Marakoopa).
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waitomo_Glowworm_Caves (North Island / Waitomo district; limestone formed ~30 Mya under the sea, Oligocene; 1300m passages, Cathedral & Glowworm Grotto; explored Dec 1887 by Tane Tinorau + Fred Mace by candlelit raft; Arachnocampa luminosa endemic to NZ; boat tour). Return of caves to Maori owners (~1989) = general knowledge, reconfirm at build.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder ('cut the lights in the Waitomo grotto and a living sky appears'). LANE BORDER (critical): geography owns the CAVE, the KARST geology, the discovery and the place — the glowworm's biology (how the larva makes light, its silk 'fishing lines') belongs to the ANIMAL bank; keep the T5 answer the PLACE-fact 'found only in New Zealand,' not anatomy. Accuracy rail: reconfirm at build — 1887 Tane Tinorau + Fred Mace, Oligocene ~30 Mya limestone, and the caves' return to Maori owners. vision_mandated: the T4 rung names a Maori chief as a full co-discoverer and celebrates Maori stewardship — frame it straight and equal, never 'exotic.' Distractors adjacent-real (other NZ caves: Ruakuri, Aranui; other karst/cave wonders). Dinner-test payoff = the living-constellation ceiling / found-only-here.

name: Light bent into an arc — rainbows & the moonbow
scope: Light bent into an arc — up to the ghost-rainbow of the moon. Spine = the rainbow, deepened across named falls and skies. T1 (a waterfall's spray — e.g. Niagara): the rainbow in the mist is sunlight BENT and bounced inside each round raindrop, which acts like a tiny prism. T2: the color order is always the same — RED on the outside, violet inside — because red light bends the least. T3: a DOUBLE rainbow's second, fainter bow has its colors REVERSED, with a dark strip between the two called Alexander's band (a named thing). T4 payoff: at Victoria Falls — Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the Smoke that Thunders,' on the Zambezi — the spray is so heavy that on a FULL-MOON night it raises a MOONBOW, a rainbow lit by moonlight instead of sunlight. T5: moonbows look ghostly WHITE to the eye because moonlight is too faint to fire our color vision (long-exposure photos reveal the colors); Cumberland Falls, Kentucky is one of the only places on Earth to see one reliably. T5+: a 'fogbow' is a near-white bow made in fog, and seen from a plane a rainbow can close into a full CIRCLE.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonbow (moonbow = rainbow from moonlight, needs near-full moon below 42 deg + spray, appears white as light is too faint for cone cells; Victoria Falls & Cumberland Falls KY reliable spots; Yosemite spray moonbows). Rainbow optics (42 deg, red outermost, Alexander's band) = standard atmospheric-optics knowledge.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder, never 'What is a rainbow?'. Accuracy rail: primary bow centered ~42 deg opposite the sun; the moonbow needs a bright low full moon + heavy spray and looks white because it is too dim for our color cells — keep those exact. RESPECT the indigenous name: pair 'Victoria Falls' with 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' plainly, no smugness, no lecture. Distractors adjacent-real (other falls: Iguazu, Angel, Yosemite; wrong optics: reflection off the water surface, sun-in-front vs sun-behind). Dinner-test payoff = the full-moon moonbow at Victoria Falls. Lane: this is OPTICS + the FALLS as a place; the Zambezi's hippos/fish are the animal bank.

name: The ice-crystal sky — sun dogs & the 22-degree halo
scope: The ice-crystal sky: false suns, rings, and pillars. Spine = light bent by hexagonal ice crystals, across cold, high places. T1 (a freezing morning on the northern plains / Fairbanks): two bright 'false suns' burn beside the real Sun — sun DOGS (parhelia). T2: they sit on a faint ring 22 degrees around the Sun — the 22-degree HALO — made by millions of six-sided ICE crystals in high, cold cirrus clouds bending the light like prisms (teach: hexagonal ice, not water drops). T3: flat plate-crystals drifting level make the dogs; column crystals stack a glowing vertical LIGHT PILLAR above city lights and low suns on frigid nights. T4 payoff: rarely a whole show appears — the circumzenithal arc, a bright 'upside-down rainbow' smiling straight overhead, purer in color than any true rainbow. T5: in 1535 the people of STOCKHOLM watched a sky crowded with sun dogs and haloes and painted it — the Vadersolstavlan, the oldest color picture of the city; a complex 1790 display over St. Petersburg gave 'Lowitz arcs' their name (observed by Johann Tobias Lowitz).
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_dog (parhelia = bright spots ~22 deg either side of sun; horizontally-oriented plate hexagonal ice crystals in cirrus/diamond dust; min deflection 22 deg; related: 22 deg halo, sun pillars, circumzenithal arc, parhelic circle; best in cold climates/low sun; 1790 St. Petersburg Lowitz arcs). Vadersolstavlan (1535 Stockholm) = well-documented artifact, reconfirm at build.
framing_note: Scene-led ('two extra suns burn beside the real one over the frozen plain'), never 'What is a sun dog?'. Accuracy rail: the halo is exactly 22 degrees and comes from HEXAGONAL ICE crystals (not water drops — that would be a rainbow); keep the 1535 Vadersolstavlan and 1790 Lowitz facts exact. Teach 'sun dog / parhelion' before testing it. Distractors adjacent-real (rainbow cause water-drops vs ice; wrong angle 42 vs 22 deg; other ice-optics: light pillar vs halo). Dinner-test payoff = the upside-down rainbow (circumzenithal arc) or the Stockholm sundog painting.

name: Water that isn't there, and cities in the air — mirages & the Fata Morgana
scope: Water that isn't there, and castles that hang in the air. Spine = light bent by layered hot and cold air, across desert, sea and Arctic. T1 (a desert highway / the Sahara): the shimmering 'pool of water' on the hot road ahead is a MIRAGE — really the blue SKY, reflected upward by a layer of super-heated air hugging the ground (an inferior mirage). T2: over cold seas and ice the OPPOSITE happens — a 'superior' mirage lifts distant ships and coastlines UP so they seem to float above the horizon. T3 payoff: the grandest kind is the FATA MORGANA, named for the sorceress Morgan le Fay — in the Strait of MESSINA between Sicily and mainland Italy sailors watched it stack the far shore into hovering 'fairy castles.' T4: a Fata Morgana can loft and stretch a real ship on the horizon into a ghostly floating shape — one likely root of the 'Flying Dutchman' legend (label: a proposed explanation, not proof). T5: mirages have fooled explorers — in 1818 Sir John Ross turned his ships back at the 'Croker Mountains' blocking the Northwest Passage that were never there, and in 1906 Robert Peary reported 'Crocker Land' in the high Arctic that later teams chased for miles across the ice before it melted into thin air.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fata_Morgana_(mirage) (superior mirage from atmospheric duct/temperature inversion, stacks/inverts distant objects; named for Morgan le Fay, Strait of Messina 'fairy castles'; Croker Mountains 1818 Ross / Parry disproved 1819; Crocker Land 1906 Peary, MacMillan 1913 chase; distinct from inferior/desert mirage). Flying Dutchman link = commonly cited explanation.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder, never 'What is a mirage?'. Accuracy rail: an inferior mirage is reflected SKY (not evaporating water); a Fata Morgana is a SUPERIOR mirage from a temperature inversion/ducting — keep the two straight, and label the Flying Dutchman a possible explanation, not fact. Distractors adjacent-real (reflection off real water; ordinary heat-haze; wrong mirage type). Dinner-test payoff = the Fata Morgana 'fairy castles' of Messina, or the phantom Crocker Land explorers chased. Lane note in history_overlap.
history_overlap: Light: the Croker Mountains (1818, Ross) and Crocker Land (1906, Peary) brush Arctic-exploration history — key the ANSWER to the OPTICAL phenomenon (a mirage), never to an expedition date/person, so no history-bank rung is duplicated.

name: The last green blink of the Sun — the green flash
scope: The last green blink of the Sun. T1 (sunset over the ocean — Hawaii, the California coast, Key West): in the final second as the Sun's rim sinks into the sea on a clear evening, its top edge can flash GREEN — the 'green flash.' T2: the air bends sunlight like a weak PRISM and separates its colors; the blue is scattered away, so a rim of GREEN is the last light left at the horizon (refraction plus dispersion). T3 payoff: at the SOUTH POLE the Sun crawls so slowly along the horizon that Admiral Byrd's crew watched a green flash come and go, on and off, for about 35 MINUTES; the sight so haunted people that Jules Verne's 1882 novel 'Le Rayon Vert' (The Green Ray) made it a charm that lets you read a true heart.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_flash (green spot at sun's upper rim at sunset/sunrise; atmosphere refracts + disperses, blue scattered out by Rayleigh so green remains; best over unobstructed ocean horizon; Byrd's Little America ~35-minute polar display; Jules Verne 1882 The Green Ray; inferior-mirage & mock-mirage types).
framing_note: Scene-led wonder ('watch the Sun's last rim slip into the Pacific'), never 'What is the green flash?'. Accuracy rail: it needs a clean, low horizon (best over the sea); it is green because blue is scattered out — the Sun does not 'turn green.' Anchor every rung to a place (an ocean horizon; the South Pole). Distractors adjacent-real (other twilight effects; wrong cause: a green cloud, an eye afterimage, pollution). Dinner-test payoff = the 35-minute polar green flash at the South Pole (Byrd).

name: The highest clouds on Earth — noctilucent clouds
scope: The highest clouds on Earth, glowing after dark. T1 (a summer midnight far north — Scotland, Scandinavia): long after sunset, electric-blue wisps shine in the deep twilight — 'night-shining' (noctilucent) clouds. T2 payoff: they float about 80 km up in the MESOSPHERE — far higher than any other cloud (jets cruise near 10 km) — so they still catch sunlight from below the horizon after the ground has gone dark. T3: first recorded in 1885, two years after KRAKATOA's 1883 eruption, and best seen between about 50 and 70 degrees latitude in summer twilight. T4: they are the tiniest ice crystals, freezing onto specks of meteor dust at the edge of space; NASA's AIM satellite (launched 2007) was built to study them, and they may be spreading as extra methane makes ice form higher up.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noctilucent_cloud (ice crystals ~76-85 km, higher than any other cloud; visible only in twilight when observer is in shadow but clouds still sunlit; first recorded 1885 two years after Krakatoa; seen ~50-70 deg latitude in summer; NASA AIM 2007; methane/water-vapor link).
framing_note: Scene-led wonder, never 'What are noctilucent clouds?'. Invert: the glow-after-dark hook -> 'they are so high (~80 km) they are still in sunlight.' Accuracy rail: mesosphere ~76-85 km (the highest clouds), first seen 1885 after Krakatoa, ice-on-meteor-dust — keep exact. Distractors adjacent-real (ordinary high cirrus; aurora; the wrong altitude). Anchor to high-latitude places (Scotland/Scandinavia/Canada). Dinner-test payoff = the highest clouds on Earth, still sunlit at midnight.

name: The pink fire on the mountains — alpenglow & the Belt of Venus
scope: The pink fire on the mountains. T1 (the Alps / Mont Blanc at dusk): after the Sun has set and the valleys are already dark, the highest snowy peaks blush PINK and orange — 'alpenglow.' T2: true alpenglow is INDIRECT light — the Sun is already below the horizon, and its reddened light bounces off the sky and haze back onto the peaks (not direct sunlight striking them). T3: turn away from the sunset and a pink band with a blue-grey base rises over the far horizon — the Belt of VENUS, sitting on top of Earth's own shadow. T4 payoff: in the DOLOMITES the glow has its own name, enrosadira ('turning rosy'); a Ladin legend says it is the enchanted rose garden of King Laurin, a dwarf-king, blooming red across the peaks at dusk (label: legend, not fact).
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpenglow (reddish glow near the horizon opposite the Sun when the disk is just below it; strict = indirect sunlight reflected/diffracted by atmosphere after sunset, soft shadows; loose usage = direct reddened light; Belt of Venus = pinkish band opposite the Sun above the anti-solar horizon; Italian term 'enrosadira'). King Laurin / Ladin legend of the Dolomites = well-known folk legend, reconfirm at build.
framing_note: Scene-led wonder ('the summits burn pink while the valley goes dark'), never 'What is alpenglow?'. Accuracy rail: TRUE alpenglow is indirect, post-sunset backscattered light — distinguish it from ordinary direct sunset-reddening; and enrosadira / King Laurin's rose garden is a LEGEND — label it, do not state as fact (reconfirm the Ladin legend at build). Distractors adjacent-real (direct sunset light; Belt of Venus vs alpenglow; other ranges: Himalaya/Aoraki/Rockies). Dinner-test payoff = the Dolomites' enrosadira / King Laurin's rose garden. A cultural creation born of that place — treat the Ladin legend with respect.
